title: Luka Doncic's Body Transformation Impresses NBA Insiders: 'As Lean As He's Been Since His Rookie Year' - NewsBreak
text:
By Chaitanya Dadhwal ,
14 minutes ago Luka Doncic sounds confident he’ll lead the Lakers toward championship contention this season. Beyond being mentally ready, he also looks physically fit.
NBA insiders Brian Windhorst and Tim McMahon invited Dave McMenamin of ESPN to their podcast, ‘The Hoop Collective,’ and, among several topics, discussed Luka Doncic’s impressive body transformation heading into training camp.
“By the way, as a quick aside, Dave, I want to report to you that Luka might be in better shape this year than he was last year,” Brian Windhorst said.
“That’s a great sign for the Lakers; that’s fantastic,” Dave McMenamin responded.
“I do think Luka is as lean as he’s been since his rookie year. Luka, I think, was listed at 218 in his rookie year, probably was legitimately like 230-ish, and he looks like he’s in about that range now,” Tim McMahon said.
“Well, we’ll see if he has the lift, right? Because back when you covered him early on in his career, he was playing above the rim a bunch,” McMenamin said. “That’s a huge development, and obviously it looked like it from, you know, the film and photos I’ve seen.”

“But it’s one thing for a guy like Luka to go on this regimented diet and workout plan last summer to get a contract extension, but if he’s in better shape now than he was last summer to secure that bag, that’s a great sign for the Lakers,” he further added.
“Luka also could have shown up to sign his extension, double-fisting steins of beer, weighing 320 lbs, and still would have gotten it,” McMahon hilariously said.
Even a post from the Lakers’ Media Day went viral on social media, where Luka Doncic looked leaner and like he had added significant muscle this summer.
The Lakers fans flooded social media, excited that their superstar looked even better than in his rookie season.
A major part of this transformation can be credited not just to his trade from the Mavericks (reportedly pushed because Dallas was concerned about his health ) but also to his contract extension with the Lakers , which kicked in this season.
In his previous physical state , Luka Doncic finished fourth in the NBA’s MVP voting despite leading the league in scoring. He finished the 2025-26 regular season averaging 33.5 points, 8.3 assists, and 7.7 rebounds while shooting 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from beyond the arc.
With Doncic seemingly in better shape than he has been in years, expectations are sky-high entering the 2026-27 season. His transformation could improve his conditioning, explosiveness, and durability while maintaining his elite production.
If that translates to the court, Luka Doncic could lead the Lakers into legitimate championship contention.
